title: A kicked ball on level ground
stem: A ball is kicked from level ground with a speed of 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. Ignore air resistance unless stated, and take g = 9.8 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the time of flight of the ball.
markscheme: vertical component u_y = 20 sin 30° = 10 m s⁻¹
parts.notes: Allow use of s = u_y t − ½gt² with s = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the horizontal range of the ball.
markscheme: horizontal component u_x = 20 cos 30° = 17.3 m s⁻¹

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine the maximum height reached by the ball.
markscheme: at the top v_y = 0 / use v² = u² − 2gh

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Air resistance is now taken into account. Explain how the trajectory of the ball changes.
markscheme: drag opposes the velocity / acts opposite to the direction of motion
horizontal velocity decreases during the flight (no longer constant)
upward deceleration is greater than g, so maximum height is lower
path is no longer symmetric / descent is steeper than ascent

title: Flywheel and clutch
stem: A flywheel of moment of inertia 0.80 kg m² starts from rest. A constant net torque of 4.0 N m acts on it for 6.0 s and is then removed. The flywheel is then coupled to a second, initially stationary disc of moment of inertia 0.40 kg m² on the same axle, and they rotate together. Friction at the bearings can be neglected.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the angular velocity of the flywheel at the end of the 6.0 s.
parts.notes: Allow angular impulse method: τΔt = IΔω.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the rotational kinetic energy of the flywheel at this time.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine the common angular velocity after the second disc is coupled.
markscheme: angular momentum conserved / no external torque: 0.80 × 30 = 24 kg m² s⁻¹

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Show that rotational kinetic energy is not conserved during the coupling, and suggest where the energy goes.
markscheme: 240 J < 360 J, so 120 J of kinetic energy is lost
energy dissipated as internal/thermal energy (and sound) by friction in the clutch while the surfaces slip
parts.notes: The coupling is the rotational analogue of a perfectly inelastic collision.
